# random2

A monorepo of installable mini-games (PWAs) and two analysis tools. Every
web project runs entirely in the browser, works offline once installed, uses
zero binary art assets (everything is drawn procedurally) and zero trackers.

## Portfolio

`portfolio/` — a bilingual EN/IT portfolio page presenting nine projects as
case studies (problem, constraint, approach, result) rather than as a list of
things to play: `census-pwa`, `stats-pwa`, `bucio`, `sector7-pwa`,
`ironfall-pwa`, `pulse-pwa`, the Monte-Carlo balance harness, the shared
engine, and the EADS embedded debugger. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no
dependencies, and unlike every other page here it loads no shared library. Its
screenshots are generated by `portfolio/scripts/shots.mjs`, which drives a
Chromium over the DevTools Protocol using only Node built-ins.

`portfolio/cv.html` is the one-page CV. It prints to exactly one A4 sheet and
its numbers carry the same `data-claim` attributes the ledger checks, so a
figure on the CV is verified as carefully as a figure on the portfolio.

### Services and availability

Three things, because three things is what the work above actually is:
interface work (screens, components, a design system in CSS custom
properties, bilingual markup), performance and accessibility audits (measured
against the WCAG formula, with the failures left in the report), and
offline-first PWA builds (manifest, service worker, precache, install).

Where, time zone, day rate and engagement shape are the only facts the
repository cannot answer: they live in `portfolio/index.html` under
`#services` and in `portfolio/now.html`, marked `data-fill-text`, and they
ship visibly unfinished until they are filled in.

### Other pages

| Page | What it is |
|---|---|
| `portfolio/cv.html` | One-page CV, prints to exactly one A4 sheet |
| `portfolio/verify.html` | The claims ledger, generated |
| `portfolio/audit/report.html` | The self-audit, generated, with the failures in it |
| `portfolio/now.html` | What is shipping this month |
| `portfolio/notes/` | Three short bilingual essays |
| `portfolio/404.html` | The portfolio's own not-found page |

### The self-audit

`tools/audit/` loads every project in this repository in a real browser over
the DevTools Protocol and checks it there: contrast ratios computed with the
WCAG formula, tap targets under 48px, controls with no accessible name, form
controls with no label, heading order, duplicate ids, and the two navigation
timings from a cold cache. The report is committed at
`portfolio/audit/report.html` with the failures in it. Both scripts skip
cleanly when there is no browser.

```bash
node tools/audit/run.mjs            # both audits, then the report
```

### The claims ledger

Every number the portfolio states is machine-checked. `tools/verify.mjs`
recomputes each one from the repository and compares it with the number the
page actually renders; if a claim drifts, CI fails. Numbers on the page carry
a `data-claim` attribute, so the comparison is against the page itself.
Numbers written in prose are covered by a stale-literal lint. The ledger is
published at `portfolio/verify.html`, and every row carries the shell command
that reproduces its number.

```bash
node tools/verify.mjs --check    # exit 1 if any claim drifted
node tools/verify.mjs --audit    # run every command and compare it
```

The house rule this enforces: a claim is only true if the ledger says so. Do
not type a number onto the page without adding it to the registry in the same
change.

## Analysis and statistics

| Project | What it is |
|---|---|
| `stats-pwa/` | Local play-data dashboard: reads every game's localStorage and draws score distributions, best-over-time, hour-by-weekday playtime heatmaps. Pure Canvas 2D, no dependencies. JSON export/import. |
| `census-pwa/` | A sampling-theory tycoon. Real margin of error, real selective non-response. `sim.js` is DOM-free and unit-tested. |
| `tools/balance/` | Monte-Carlo balance harness: Node drives `metro-pwa/sim.js` headless over 5000 seeded sessions; Python (stdlib only) writes an HTML report with inline SVG charts. |
| `tools/corpora/` | Corpus statistics over the literary PWAs' own bilingual prose: sentence lengths, type/token ratio, hapax legomena, Zipf fits, EN/IT overlap. |

## Notable games

`pulse-pwa/` is a four-lane rhythm game with no audio files. One 32-bit seed decides
tempo, key, chord progression, drum pattern and a melodic motif; the note chart is
read back out of the same melody, so chart and audio cannot disagree. The track is
rendered offline in twelve-second chunks and scheduled as each chunk finishes, so it
is playable in about 450 ms with nothing downloaded. `src/song.js` and `src/chart.js`
are DOM-free and deterministic, which is what lets the generator be tested over 500
seeds in Node.

`pixel-cup-pwa/` is a low-poly arcade football game whose picture is neither
WebGL nor images: the pitch, the players, the ball, the goal and the crowd are
triangles drawn by hand into a 320x180 byte buffer that the browser scales up
with nearest-neighbour sampling. Faces are flat-shaded and quantised to a
limited palette, which is what makes them read as low-poly rather than as a
small smooth render, and the rasteriser tests 1/d against a depth buffer -
1/d being an exact affine function of the screen position across a plane, so
interpolating it across a triangle is not an approximation and the pitch, the
players and the goalposts share one buffer with no sorting at all. The rules
live in a DOM-free `core.js` that the browser and the Node tests load
unchanged, and the balance is pinned by those tests: a scripted player of
ordinary ability has to score, the opposition has to score too, and a match
has to land between one and a half and seven goals. Every sound is
synthesised, so there is not one audio file in the folder.

## Shared libraries

`shared/arcade.js` — WebAudio blips, particles, localStorage helpers, seeded
RNG (`dailySeed`, `mulberry32`), playtime tracking, and the `R2.stats` run log.

`shared/chart.js` — zero-dependency Canvas 2D charts: line, area, bar,
histogram, scatter, boxplot, heatmap, sparkline. DPR-aware, honours
`prefers-reduced-motion`, reads colours from CSS custom properties so it
follows the hub's theme toggle.

## Testing

```
node tools/selftest.mjs        # shared libraries
node metro-pwa/sim.test.mjs    # LINEA ROSSA sim
node census-pwa/sim.test.mjs    # CENSUS sim
python3 tools/balance/test.py  # balance report
python3 tools/corpora/test.py  # corpus statistics
node pulse-pwa/sim.test.mjs    # PULSE generator + chart
node stats-pwa/smoke.mjs       # in-browser (skips if no playwright)
node census-pwa/smoke.mjs      # in-browser (skips if no playwright)
node pulse-pwa/smoke.mjs       # in-browser (skips if no playwright)
node pixel-cup-pwa/sim.test.mjs  # PIXEL CUP '96 model
node pixel-cup-pwa/boot.test.mjs # PIXEL CUP '96, the whole game on a fake DOM
node pixel-cup-pwa/smoke.mjs      # in-browser (skips if no playwright)
```

## Layout

Each PWA is a plain static folder: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `game.js`,
`manifest.json`, `service-worker.js`, `icons/`. No build step, no bundler.
The bigger games use a `src/` of classic scripts under one `window.<NS>`
namespace instead of a single `game.js` - `ironfall-pwa/` is the reference for
that shape. `bucio/` (Vite + three.js) and `new-star-soccer/` (Vite +
TypeScript) are the exceptions.
